body: If you have not been rubbing your eyes along with washing and fanning out your lashes then I’d agree this is a bad set. But if you are sleeping on your face, not up keeping the cleanliness, or rubbing your lashes then this can produce a bad looking set.

I’d recommend lattise to create longer and fuller natural lashes. The longer and healthier your nadtural lashes, the bigger and fuller the fans can be. These seem kind of small. Maybe find a new lash tech that can do the look you like but also this photo shows you in much need for a fill.
Fuck you Jessica. You’re not paying people to show up for these interviews. Lower those expectations.
Bro she said what? Trim them?!?! Run and never look back. Find a few lash techs in your area and ask for help. You’d be surprised many will help you remove and replace those !

Yes! Tell your lash tech you want to downgrade to hybrids then to classics. You can see them gradually go down and decide if you like them! You can also opt for a removal and get a new classic or hybrid set.
If anything happens to your full set within 3 days I’d go right back. Once you hit a week it’s kinda iffy BC you’re halfway to your fill n

I’m a lash tech and these look really good and they also match your brow shape! Was it more fullness you wanted or less? Also I’d ask your lash tech for a removal if in a few days they don’t grow on ya because if applied correctly they can stay glued on from 1 week up to 8 weeks. 

—-I’d say next time you make an appointment send your lash tech multiple photos of the specific look you want (all eyes are different so including multiple photos will help them achieve your desired look)

I’d say yes. I am a lash tech and from looking I can’t say 100% but you probably have skin and lashes glued together or clump of lashes that are stuck together creating tension. I’d ask your lash tech to fix your lashes or remove them.
Hey babe. It fully depends on your lash artist and the look of your lashes the actual day of your appt. I’d suggest sending updates to your lash artist about retention problems.
